lessons.explain: Catholic English vẫn là tiếng Anh, nhưng một số từ mang nghĩa chuyên biệt. Church có thể chỉ Giáo hội; church có thể chỉ nhà thờ. Chữ hoa là dấu hiệu hữu ích, nhưng phải đọc cả câu. Faith thường là đức tin, không chỉ là sự tin tưởng vào khả năng của ai đó.

lessons.reading: My name is An. I am a candidate living in a Catholic community in Vietnam. We study, pray, and share daily responsibilities. On Sundays, I help welcome visitors at a local parish. Some visitors speak English, so I am learning how to introduce myself and explain our activities clearly. I do not need to know every theological word before I can greet someone kindly. When a word is unfamiliar, I ask for an explanation rather than pretend to understand. A respectful question can begin a useful conversation.

lessons.reading: During an English study session, Linh sees the sentence, 'The Church serves people in many places.' She first imagines a building. Her partner explains that Church here refers to the community of believers, not just a physical place. Later, they read that the church opens at six. This time, the sentence refers to a building. lessons.reading: A study group is learning to use Bible references. The leader writes Mark 4:35-41 on the board. The group first identifies the book, then the chapter, and finally the verses. They read the surrounding passage before discussing individual words. A participant notices that a reference helps everyone find the same place even when page numbers differ between editions. The leader asks each person to distinguish what the passage says from a personal response to it. The group uses an approved published translation rather than creating a new translation for prayer.

lessons.reading: Mai prepares a short presentation about reading Scripture. Her teacher asks her to notice whether a passage is a poem, a narrative, or a letter. These forms do not communicate in exactly the same way. Mai begins her summary with the setting and the people involved, then states the main point in her own words. She avoids treating every image as a literal description. When she is unsure, she consults a reliable commentary and notes its source. Her summary is a learning aid, not a replacement for the biblical text or the Church's interpretation.

Students record both the specialist meaning and a practical sentence to avoid using the term as an empty label.
